# Governance Fundamentals

Regular portrait-mode content goes here — write normally, exactly as you did in Typora. Plain headings, lists, bold/italic, images, and narrow tables all work with no special syntax.

Here is a normal narrow table (fine in portrait). These definitions align with the foundational framework in @Smith:2021qr.

**Core risk terminology**

```{=latex}
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.25\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.65\linewidth}
@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\textbf{Term} & \textbf{Definition} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Asset & Something of value \\
Risk & Potential for loss \\
\caption{Definitions referenced throughout this book.}
\phantomsection\label{tbl-terms}
\end{longtable}
```

## Example: wide table in landscape with header, first-column, and row shading

When a table has many columns and needs more horizontal room, wrap it in a landscape block. Only this table's page rotates — everything before and after stays portrait.

Pandoc's auto-generated tables (from Markdown pipe syntax) can't shade just the header row or just one column — only whole-row zebra striping via `\rowcolors`. For that level of control, write the table directly in raw LaTeX instead, using `\cellcolor` per cell (it overrides whatever `\rowcolor` set for that row). The header/ first-column colors below are the brand-defined `giTable...` colors from `preamble.tex`, with a hairline `giTableDivider` rule between rows instead of alternating-row shading — combining zebra striping *and* rules on the same table tends to look busy/competing; picking one is cleaner. (Zebra striping is still available via `\rowcolor` if you'd rather have it back instead of the dividers — just swap which one runs between the data rows below.)

The control register methodology follows @Smith:2022jd.

**Sample requirements register**

```{=latex}
\begin{landscape}
\giLandscapeHeader

{
% Column widths are weighted by expected content length, not equal —
% "Requirement" holds full sentences and needs the most room; short
% fields like "Status" or "Risk Level" only need enough for one word.
% Pandoc's auto-generated tables always use equal-width columns; this
% is why this table is written as raw LaTeX rather than a Markdown
% pipe table. Weights below sum to 1.0 — adjust them to match your
% own columns' typical content length, not their header length.
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 16\tabcolsep) * \real{0.09}} % Control ID
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 16\tabcolsep) * \real{0.10}} % Domain
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 16\tabcolsep) * \real{0.28}} % Requirement
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 16\tabcolsep) * \real{0.14}} % Evidence Type
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 16\tabcolsep) * \real{0.10}} % Frequency
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 16\tabcolsep) * \real{0.11}} % Owner
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 16\tabcolsep) * \real{0.09}} % Risk Level
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 16\tabcolsep) * \real{0.09}} % Status
@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\rowcolor{giTableHeaderShade}
\textbf{Control ID} & \textbf{Domain} & \textbf{Requirement} & \textbf{Evidence Type} & \textbf{Frequency} & \textbf{Owner} & \textbf{Risk Level} & \textbf{Status} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\cellcolor{giTableFirstColShade}REQ-001 & Governance & Board reviews policy annually & Meeting minutes & Annual & Owner A & High & Active \\
\arrayrulecolor{giTableDivider}\hline
\cellcolor{giTableFirstColShade}REQ-002 & Access & MFA enforced on all admin accounts & Config export & Continuous & Owner B & High & Active \\
\arrayrulecolor{giTableDivider}\hline
\cellcolor{giTableFirstColShade}REQ-003 & Data & Data classified per policy & Classification log & Quarterly & Owner C & Medium & Active \\
\arrayrulecolor{giTableDivider}\hline
\cellcolor{giTableFirstColShade}REQ-004 & Incident & IR plan tested & Test report & Annual & Owner D & High & Active \\
\caption{Sample requirements register, mapped to evidence type and
review frequency.}
\phantomsection\label{tbl-controls}
\end{longtable}
}

\giLandscapeFooter
\end{landscape}
```

Portrait content resumes right after the landscape table. Tables labeled `tbl-*` are cross-referenceable elsewhere in the text — for example, @tbl-terms and @tbl-controls above resolve automatically to "Table 2.1" / "Table 2.2" and stay correct even if the tables get reordered or renumbered later.

*Table headers* (the bold line right above a table, like "Sample requirements register" above) are just an ordinary bold paragraph — no special syntax needed, works the same for both Markdown and raw-LaTeX tables. *Captions* need raw LaTeX either way: Pandoc's native Markdown table caption syntax (a `:` line after the table) always renders the caption **above** the table, with no way to move it — that's hardcoded in Pandoc's template, not something this project's styling controls. To get a caption below the table (as both tables on this page do), write the table as raw LaTeX and place `\caption{}\label{}` near the end, right before `\end{longtable}` — and make sure the table is **not** wrapped in `\def\LTcaptype{none}` (that's Pandoc's own convention for suppressing numbering on *uncaptioned* tables; a captioned table needs it removed, or the caption won't number or show up in the List of Tables). Citations don't resolve inside a raw LaTeX block (Quarto's citation processor only sees actual Markdown text), so keep any `@citekey` in the surrounding prose rather than inside the `\caption{}` text itself.
